step: LONG-TAIL BATCH C, FIX 2 - the item announcement is a MOVE's own `onTryHit` (battle-actions.ts:1044, inside spreadMoveHit) and this engine emitted it beside `onTry`, above every hit-step gate
what_changed: engine/medicham2-browser.js (the emission moved out of the onTry precondition block into a new `_stepAnnounceItem` in the step list, beside `_stepClearScreens`; one knob, one counter)
which_scoreboard: PROTOCOL. A refused click deals the same damage either way - none - so no board leaf can move. Said before the run: BOARD-MATERIAL sits exactly still.

prediction.reasoning: 7 rows of the FULL by-cause list name this line - counted over `classes`, not over `state.first_board_divergences`, which is capped at 40 and is not the population. The struggle fix in the same batch closed 14 of its 17 rows outright and re-classified 3, an 82% close rate; 7 x 0.82 = 5.7, so I call SIX closing and ONE re-classifying onto a divergence behind it. 137 - 6 = 131. The risk is in the other direction from struggle: a Poltergeist is clicked EARLY, so there are more turns left in which a second defect can surface, and I would not be surprised by 132 or 133.

counters.MEDSEEN.targetItemAnnounced: > 0 - the line is still written on connected clicks, and it must now be STRICTLY FEWER than before, because the refused ones stopped writing it

how_a_miss_would_read: board_material moving at all means an announcement that could not touch a leaf did. protocol falling by MORE than 7 means something closed this fix cannot explain. protocol falling by fewer than 4 means most of these games carry a second defect and the bucket was smaller than its row count.
